findings.title: Keep display-only source scope out of retailer search queries
findings.description: Adding source_scope_label to the shared lineLabel helper changes more than displayed text. backingLineOffer uses that helper to overwrite a generic-search offer's retailer query, so historical/catalog/stock prose now becomes literal Amazon search terms. Plain row IDs are preserved, but the shopping action no longer uses only the product identity and strength described by that function's contract.
findings.trigger: On a line page, select a source-scoped mainline row as backing and calculate a successful plan with positive backing yards whose offer falls back to generic_search.
findings.impact: Provenance such as '2014 US catalog' or 'stock unverified' unnecessarily constrains a product search. This is an observable outbound-query regression, not a stylistic concern. The exact effect on live retailer search results was not tested.
findings.reproductionMethod: Read baseline engine with git show 045b091:js/line-page-engine.js and current engine from disk. Run each production engine in a separate Node VM with the same current catalog and affiliate mappings; expose backingLineOffer only in memory. Pass assessmentTone=success, needsBacking=true, backingYards=40 and each exact backing row, then decode the returned Amazon k parameter.

findings.recommendedFix: Retain the scoped helper for visible text. Construct the generic backing search from plain brand, model, strength and normalized type, without source_scope_label. Do not remove source qualifications from displays or change reviewed row identities.
findings.regressionTest: For scoped and unscoped backing rows, assert that visible labels include the appropriate qualification but decoded retailer queries exclude provenance prose and retain plain product identity/strength. Cover the generic_search path, which the current label-focused cross-tool fixtures do not exercise.
